units.text: The assertion is supported: Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863, in Washington, D.C. Evidence from the National Archives (77178600-9a10-4568-8bf6-0a95c58b198c, adfdefc5-59d1-4ec7-ac13-7dc54ab04d63) and National Bell Festival source (4a2577dc-3679-4d20-9239-541bcf7779d1),

citations.title: What is the Emancipation Proclamation? | National Bell Festival

judgement.reason: The passages support that Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863, but none mention Washington, D.C. as the location.

units.text: The full text of the Proclamation, as cited in National Archives transcript (77178600-9a10-4568-8bf6-0a95c58b198c, 704a23d3-66ef-4051-bca0-92a9e1fd961e), reads that it was 'Done at the City of Washington, this first day of January, in the year of our Lord one thousand eight hundred and sixty-three.'

citations.title: Myths & Misunderstandings: The Emancipation Proclamation Archives- American Civil War Museum

judgement.reason: The provided passages do not contain the quoted closing phrase 'Done at the City of Washington...' nor the cited transcript identifiers, so they do not support the statement.

units.text: No evidence contradicts the date, location, or the act of issuance by Lincoln on that date from the capital.

judgement.reason: The first passage supports the date (January 1, 1863) and that Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation, but neither passage mentions the location or that it was issued from the capital, so that part is unsupported.
